description: It woke in warm grass with a life of sea ice behind it, and grew its own back. The tusks are that same ice.
lore: It woke where everything wakes: in the meadow grass, in warm air, within sight of the house and the fire, with a whole life of frozen sea behind it and no ice anywhere it could see. There is a courtesy for that hour — you sit with the newly woken and ask their name and one true thing. Nobody has worked out how to do that for something with no name to give. It stood up on its own and went north, and kept going north, and there is nothing that far north but weather.

The ice came afterwards, and it came out of the bear. The crystals stand up through the coat at the shoulders and will not melt — not in rain, not in a warm month, not held in a hand. The tusks are the same stuff, grown down past a jaw with no business growing anything. It carries its own winter because there was not one here to be had.

And it walks toward fires. That is the whole trouble with it: a bear goes by smell and warmth, and a tended fire is the warmest, best-smelling thing this country has. So every so often the cold arrives before the animal does, and a keeper looks up to find a great pale shape sitting just outside the light, not coming nearer, not going. [[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] has had one sit out three of her nights this year. She has taken to setting something down past the stones before she starts, which is in no rota she was ever given. She will not call it a prayer. She says so quickly, more than once, and she has not missed a night since it started coming.
gm_notes: Description replaced: the shipped line ("carved by the glacier and jealous of it") reads Made, and this one is Come — an animal that arrived like everyone else. Law I demonstrated from the wrong end: the meeting-courtesy has no procedure for an arrival with no name. Jehanne's feeding is the joke that turns — a woman who cannot stop practising, adding an unauthorised rite for a bear and denying it is one.
